note: Shared framework capabilities that the gated service families need, grouped so the runtime owner can size one capability instead of eighteen service exceptions. Each group lists the services that need it, the documented requirement per service, and the minimal synthetic contract that would let a framework-side wire test prove the capability without a live account. Nothing here is a connector instruction: no connector may work around these limits.

groups.title: Reviewed static request headers
groups.engine_limit: Request headers are limited to Authorization, Accept and Content-Type plus at most one reviewed operation-ID header, so a service that requires its own header on every request cannot be reached at all.

requirements.documented: Every request must carry a Notion-Version header; requests without it are rejected.
Personal access tokens are passed in the X-Figma-Token header rather than in Authorization.
Recommended for production code and echoed back on responses; v3 is also the current default.
Every OCS call must carry this header, and Accept: application/json selects the JSON representation.

fixture_contract.description: One identity GET, one read GET and one reviewed write POST per service, each recorded with the exact header set the transport must send.

samples.identity: no documented identity endpoint; a bot-user or parent-page lookup is a data read
samples.write_request: POST /v1/pages with the nested v3 template already implemented
samples.proves: the required header is present on every method and the reviewed payload is unchanged

samples.identity: GET /v1/me returning id, handle and an email documented only on that endpoint
samples.write_request: none claimed; Figma is read-only in this queue
samples.proves: a non-Bearer token header is carried without weakening the Bearer parser

samples.write_request: none claimed; revisions need separate acceptance
samples.proves: an optional version header and a root-array collection can both be read

samples.identity: GET /ocs/v1.php/cloud/user returning an XML or JSON OCS envelope
samples.proves: a mandatory non-auth header and an envelope body are handled without weakening origin rules

unblocks: Notion profiles once sign-in is accepted
a Figma personal-token read subset
a Zotero library read subset
a Nextcloud OCS share subset on an approved host

groups.title: Offset, page-number, keyset, Link-header and nextLink paging
groups.engine_limit: Only bounded cursor pagination through one reviewed query parameter is followed, so a service that pages any other way returns only its first page and says nothing about the rest.

requirements.documented: List endpoints return a Link header with rel=next rather than a cursor field.
Collections page with page/per_page and return X-Next-Page and Link headers.
Collections return @odata.nextLink as an absolute URL and @odata.nextLink must be followed to continue.
List records return an opaque offset string that is sent back as the offset parameter.
Collections page with page and perpage, where perpage is capped at 50.
Responses carry pagination.next_page as a full URL or null.
Collections page with a next_page token passed in the request.
Paging uses offset and limit query parameters.
Notes use page and limit, while /events uses a cursor property.
limit and start offsets plus an HTTP Link header with rel=next.
Task lists are documented as capped at 100 tasks per page; the exact mechanism is not verified here.
Cursor paging already matches the reviewed cursor contract: pageCursor in, nextPageCursor out. This service is gated on authentication and identity, not paging.

fixture_contract.description: Two synthetic pages per service plus the documented stop signal: the first page with its continuation marker and the second page with the marker absent, so a framework test can prove both that a second page is fetched and that the stop is honoured.

samples.page_one: an issue array plus a Link header with rel=next
samples.page_two: an issue array with no rel=next link
samples.proves: Link-header paging advances and stops without following a host outside the origin

samples.page_one: a value array plus @odata.nextLink pointing at the same origin
samples.proves: an absolute nextLink on the reviewed origin is followed once and bounded

samples.page_one: a records array plus an offset string
samples.page_two: a records array with no offset
samples.proves: an opaque offset is echoed back unchanged and bounded

unblocks: GitLab issue listing for a selected project
GitHub repository issue listing for the pinned repository

Airtable, Raindrop, Spotify, Asana, Calendly and Zotero listing subsets

groups.title: Non-Bearer token schemes and credential placement
groups.engine_limit: Only Authorization: Bearer is accepted, and a credential may never appear in a path or query, so documented Token, bare-token, key-and-token and query-parameter schemes cannot be carried.

requirements.documented: Authorization: Token <token>, not Bearer.
A personal token is sent as a bare Authorization header value with no scheme prefix; OAuth access tokens are currently non-expiring.
Key and token are sent as query parameters, as a non-standard OAuth header, or in a request body; a new OAuth 2.0 route uses Bearer with PKCE.
The token is a required query parameter on every call to the local server.
WebDAV uses Basic authentication or session cookies; OCS also accepts an OIDC bearer token.
Access tokens are OAuth only; there is no documented personal token.

fixture_contract.description: A credential-shape sample per scheme that proves the token never reaches a path, a query, a log or a task result, and that a rejected scheme fails before dispatch rather than being retried with Bearer.

samples.credential: an opaque token with no Bearer prefix
samples.proves: a non-Bearer scheme and an identity-less probe are handled without guessing an account
the token is not silently prefixed with Bearer

samples.credential: an OAuth 2.0 access token used with Bearer
samples.identity: GET /1/members/me returning id, username and an optional full name
samples.proves: the OAuth 2.0 route works without the legacy key and token

unblocks: a Readwise Reader subset once identity can be established
a ClickUp subset for one approved token type only
a Trello subset through OAuth 2.0

groups.title: Application-level success flags
groups.engine_limit: Only the HTTP status decides success, so a documented HTTP 200 carrying a failure flag would be reported to a task as a completed action.

requirements.documented: Web API methods answer HTTP 200 with ok:false and an error field for application errors, so a status-only check would call a failed send a success.
Responses carry a result boolean alongside the HTTP status.
OCS answers HTTP 200 with meta.status and meta.statuscode, where 100 means success.

fixture_contract.description: A success body and a failure body per service that both arrive with HTTP 200, so a test can prove only the success body is reported as applied and the failure body is surfaced as a failure.

samples.proves: ok:false is never reported as a successful send
result:false is never reported as a successful write

unblocks: any Slack subset, which must also gain reviewed channel destinations
Raindrop.io bookmark creation
Nextcloud OCS writes

groups.title: Account identity beyond one subject string and one label
groups.engine_limit: Identity must be one GET returning HTTP 200 JSON with a usable subject string and a non-empty label string, so a URI subject, a 204 probe, an absent identity route or a nullable label cannot bind an account.

requirements.documented: The canonical user identifier is a resource URI such as https://api.calendly.com/users/AAAA, with name and slug as separate required fields.
The only documented probe is GET /api/v2/auth/, which answers 204 with no body and exposes no account identifier.
GET /v1/me returns account_id as the linkable identifier, while display_name can be null and email needs an extra scope.
GET /v0/meta/whoami returns id always, and email only when the token has user.email:read.
There is no documented current-user identity route for an integration token.
GET /v1.0/me returns id and userPrincipalName, while mail can be null for some accounts.
The API exposes no account identity at all; it serves one local profile.

fixture_contract.description: One identity document per service that shows the documented subject and label fields, including the nullable and absent cases, so a test can prove an account is bound by a stable identifier rather than a display string that can be absent.

samples.proves: a stable subject is used and a null label is surfaced rather than invented

samples.document: resource.uri as the canonical identifier plus resource.name
samples.proves: a URI subject is either accepted explicitly or rejected clearly, never truncated into a bogus id

unblocks: a Spotify read subset with a stable account identity
a Calendly identity contract once a URI subject is deliberately supported
explicitly documenting that Readwise, Notion and Joplin have no bindable identity

groups.title: Native OAuth sign-in, scope normalization and refresh
groups.engine_limit: Bearer recipes accept a token the user supplies; there is no sign-in flow, so scope normalization, refresh and expiry cannot be proven from a recipe.

requirements.documented: Delegated Graph access needs a registered application, PKCE sign-in, normalized scopes and refresh tokens.
A personal access token has no refresh and its documented syntax still needs acceptance.
Access tokens last one hour and require a refresh flow.
OAuth 2.0 access tokens last about an hour with single-use refresh tokens and PKCE S256.

fixture_contract.description: A synthetic authorization-code exchange and refresh exchange per service, so a framework test can prove that a registered client, PKCE S256, an http://127.0.0.1 callback, scope normalization and refresh all work end to end without a live account.

samples.token_response: access_token, token_type Bearer, expires_in, scope, refresh_token
samples.proves: a delegated token can be obtained, refreshed and bound to one account

groups.title: Reads that are POST requests with request objects
groups.engine_limit: Reads are GET only and writes are single POSTs whose bodies are reviewed flat bindings or templates, so an RPC or GraphQL read cannot be expressed at all.

requirements.documented: RPC-style endpoints are POST /2/... with a JSON request object such as {"path": ...} or {"cursor": ...}.
Queries and mutations are POST /graphql with a query string, variables and an application-level errors array.

fixture_contract.description: One synthetic read POST per service with its documented request object and response shape, proving a credential-bearing read body is reviewed before dispatch and that a GraphQL errors array is never reported as a successful read.

samples.request: {"path": ""} for a root list, {"cursor": ...} for a continuation
samples.proves: a POST read is reviewed like a write and its cursor is bounded
a GraphQL errors array is surfaced as a failed read

unblocks: a Dropbox file listing subset
a Linear issue listing subset

groups.title: Approved local and self-hosted service origins
groups.engine_limit: A profile origin is one exact public HTTPS domain with no port, so a local desktop API or a self-hosted instance can never be an origin, and weakening that global rule is not an option.

requirements.documented: Every instance is self-hosted at the user's own host, commonly with a non-default port.
The clipper server is local, typically http://localhost:41184.
A local API also exists on http://localhost:23119 with its own key rules.

fixture_contract.description: A local-origin sample per service plus a user approval record, proving that loopback or private-range access is possible only after an explicit per-service local approval and never by relaxing the public HTTPS rule.

samples.probe: GET /ping answering the plain string JoplinClipperServer
samples.identity: none exists; the API exposes no account
samples.proves: a local service is opt-in, loopback-only and carries no credential in a path

unblocks: a Joplin note-capture subset for users who approve a local adapter
a Nextcloud subset for users who approve their own instance

groups.title: Reconciliation of uncertain writes
groups.engine_limit: A write is dispatched once and an uncertain result is reported as uncertain with no retry, because a profile can carry at most one operation-ID header and one reviewed reconciliation lookup.

requirements.documented: Creating an issue returns no operation identifier that a later lookup could match.
A created task returns its task id, which a later read could match, but the interpreter has no reviewed post-write probe step.
Creating an issue returns the issue number and URL, which a reviewed read could confirm.
Creating a record returns the created record id, which a reviewed read could confirm.

fixture_contract.description: A dispatched-then-failed write per service followed by the documented read that proves the commit, so a test can show the difference between an uncertain outcome that is later confirmed and one that is not retried blindly.

samples.proves: a pinned repository can confirm its own create without a new capability

unblocks: a confirmed outcome instead of a manual receipt check for the shipped subsets
